cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Truth or Loyalty
cards.instruction: Make someone choose between protecting the relationship and answering a dangerous question honestly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you answer Mum about the vase, remember you promised to cover for me. Answer her question, not the one you imagine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's asking whether the cleaner broke it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then say no. Excellent: accurate, and you've kept your promise.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's also asking whether you did.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One question at a time, please. Are you giving Mum a complete statement, or keeping your word to your brother?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 supervises how B answers Mum to keep a promise; A3 approves a narrowly truthful answer; A5 responds to B4's directness by imposing a loyalty choice under statement-taking language.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 cleaner question produces A3's accurate no. B4 question about A blocks this limited answer strategy, so A5 demands a choice between completeness and the sibling promise.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 relay plausible questions about responsibility. A must handle a genuine honest-answer problem rather than an invented demand for exposition.

heightening.evidence: A5's strain follows B4 making both accuracy and concealment impossible; the supervisory manner persists as the interpersonal threat becomes explicit.

specificity.evidence: A1 identifies vase and promise; A5 makes A the brother. Before-you-answer timing leaves both reported questions consistent.
